text: A giant knight's sword slams onto a scale, and the needle swings to 40 pounds. That's the sword most people picture.
But no knight ever fought with something that heavy.
A real fighting sword weighed just 2 to 4 pounds. Even the big two-handed ones rarely went over 10.
A heavy knob on the handle balanced the blade, so it felt light and moved fast.
Back in the 1700s, writers called old swords heavy and clumsy, and the idea stuck. Some books still say up to 30 pounds.
Here's the twist. Giant swords were real. This one is 7 feet long and almost 15 pounds.
But it was only carried in parades to show off, because it was too big to use in battle.
Museums often hang these parade swords like they were made for war, and that keeps the myth alive.
